description: Regenerative Agriculture in the Arid Southwest at Oatman Flats Ranch is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. After decades of intensive horse ranching and cotton farming in the lower Gila River region, Oatman Flats Ranch transitioned from conventional to organic practices in 2018, then to regenerative agricultural practices in 2020. Coverage: Gila Bend, Arizona (2023). The toolkit gives Gila Bend, Arizona as the location, 2023 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: After decades of intensive horse ranching and cotton farming in the lower Gila River region, Oatman Flats Ranch transitioned from conventional to organic practices in 2018, then to regenerative agricultural practices in 2020. With their minimal tillage model and leverage of traditional agricultural knowledge, Oatman Flats seeks to restore balance to their land while producing crops profitably.
